page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C core with hyper-threading operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, and is bundled with 118 GB of local storage. The CPU features a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for tile and integer operations.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated in the average tier at 2215.58, whereas the multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10% at 2263.98, reflecting the physical limitation of a single core. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show weak to poor results, with large-block write speeds at 12.15 GB/sec and read speeds at 22.92 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance also rank in the bottom 25%, indicating that while memory capacity is high relative to vCPUs, throughput is constrained.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, the E2ds_v7 provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring moderate memory capacity without high compute density. It is applicable to small-scale relational databases, caching layers, and lightweight web serving where memory footprint is more critical than parallel processing power. However, the low multi-core scaling and constrained memory bandwidth make it less effective for heavy parallel computing, large-scale data analytics, or high-throughput database workloads.
